critique.summary: Front-loaded taste-targeted spend works: A3 reaches 10.1% (P10 8.6%) at $765 per point, and A2 reaches 9.1% at $862, both more than double the benchmark's 4.2% at $1903. Late street teams on day 33 and the one-day social burst on day 32 earn little, and the hair salon partner is consistently weak.

findings.finding: Best on mean (10.1%), 10th percentile (8.6%) and cost ($765/pt); 20-day social from day 0 earns 17.4% of adoption and the Target drop earns 11.5% for $2000.
Street teams on day 33 in Fort McPherson (1.0%) and Sylvan Hills (0.7%) cost $900 combined and come too late for word of mouth to spread.
The podcasts carry the plan (13.9% and 11.7% of adoption for $6750), but the $180 one-day social on day 32 earns only 1.1% and gives word of mouth no time to work.
Snob Life Studio returns only 1.0–1.1% for $300, while Fortnite, Afrobeats and streetwear districts lead at 14.6–16.3% and Pop divas and binge TV lag at 8.3–9.1%.

changes.change: In A3, drop street:1 and street:3 on day 33 and use the $900 to add the Dead Ass podcast ad (podcast:294A0E2B…) around day 5, after trimming social:city slightly to fit.
changes.why: The late street teams earn 1.7% for $900, while the podcast earned 13.9% in A2 and seeds word of mouth early.

changes.change: Replace partner Snob Life Studio (3786CFB8) with a Fort McPherson partner near zone 4 (Pop divas and binge TV).
changes.why: The salon earns about 1% in both plans, and zone 4 has 2.3% of the audience with the weakest district reach of 8.3%.

changes.change: If keeping A2, move social:city from day 32 to days 0–15.
changes.why: Front-loaded social drove A3's 17.4% share, while the day-32 burst got only 1.1%.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B2

plan.headline: Long citywide social plus Target drop reaches 10.8% of natural audience, 2.6x benchmark
plan.summary: The bet is 26 days of fit-weighted social ads across Atlanta plus a co-branded Target drop, starting 34 days out, backed by four high-affinity neighborhood partners in Atlanta University Center and Fort McPherson. Qloo taste data shows this crowd over-indexes on Target (affinity 0.95) and on soul food and arts spots drawn in by Cedric the Entertainer and Steve Harvey (affinity 0.84–0.92), so steady, fit-weighted exposure beats busy-spot street teams. The simulation projects 10.8% reach of the natural audience (range 9.5%–12.5%) at $727 per point versus 4.2% and $1903 for the benchmark, about 2.6x, with word of mouth driving roughly half of adoption; this is a simulation built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.
